newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent a lb weaker Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EST, dealers said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture put new sales for the week ended Nov 28, at a scant 80,600 bales. While weak sales were expected due to the holdiay, prices will have to come down to trigger additional sales, market sources said.
Support was pegged between 74.50 and 74.00 in March.

Additionally, the U.S. Agriculture Department attache in India said that country's cotton crop will probably fall below year-ago levels. He pegged the 1996/97 crop at 15.7 million bales. Exports were projected at 1.2 million bales, up about 30 percent from last year.
The comments released Wednesday, were taken from a report issued earlier in the week.

NYCE cotton futures settled lower Wednesday on chart-driven selling, which erased stops and pressured prices to the day's lows. March closed down 1.03 at 74.75, traded 74.35 to 73.20 The back months ended 1.07 to 0.05 weaker.
